## 6c68e1b008a5

**Actionable curriculum gap: generated lessons never exercise the deeper onion layers required by the canonical task.** The selected source is bound to SHA-256 `dfdc1d18d5aa346fac3ac346ccd8fcaa1bc7b6403567863d77aa1851b89428e7`. I exhaustively sampled 100 seeds for every one of the six declared profiles in each difficulty band (1,800 generated inputs). Every generated reference panel had width 4, maximum onion depth 2, and a two-color learned palette; every generated query also had maximum depth 2. In contrast, the three canonical pairs have reference depths 3, 4, and 4, palette sizes 3, 4, and 4, and two canonical queries require depth 3. A learner can therefore fit the generated distribution with the shortcut “only infer/apply the first two palette colors,” yet fail the canonical depth-3/4 cases.

Reproduction and exact counts: `checks/audit/6c68e1b008a5/depth-support.json`. Reproduction script: `checks/audit/6c68e1b008a5/probe_depth_support.py`.

The strict audit also found two independent verification defects rather than disproving this finding: the portable task-test preflight rejects the fixed `Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / "data/canonical/puzzles.jsonl"` lookup, and the generator declares no `strict_canonical_like`, semantic witnesses, or `lesson_identifiable` contract. Evidence: `checks/audit/6c68e1b008a5/combined/result.json` and `checks/audit/6c68e1b008a5/combined/checks/6c68e1b008a5_audit_semantic_gate.log`. I did not edit the audited generator.
